title: Inaugural meeting of the 2022–2026 council
subtitle: Swearing-in, committee chair appointments, Grand River Hospital board seat, and the mayor's inaugural address on housing and climate.
overview: Kitchener's new term of council began with a ceremonial inaugural meeting. The mayor and ten councillors were sworn in, with an Indigenous reflection, invocations from two faith leaders, a further community reflection and music from local youth groups. One councillor had already taken the oath on the first day of the term and was not at the ceremony.

The business was short. Council appointed Councillor P. Singh as the Grand River Hospital board trustee for a one-year term {{vote:m1}}, then adopted the Striking Committee report as amended {{vote:m2}}. That report sets the chairs and vice-chairs of the three standing committees, the members of quasi-judicial boards and advisory committees, and council's representatives on outside organizations. These bodies shape how planning, finance and community services decisions reach council over the term.

In the inaugural address, the mayor named housing affordability, homelessness, climate change and road safety as the top resident concerns and invited residents to take part through the strategic plan, committees and delegations. Council also passed by-laws, including one on appointing an acting mayor, before adjourning.

decisions.detail: Councillor P. Singh was appointed as council's Grand River Hospital board trustee for a one-year term ending November 14, 2023, amending the Striking Committee report.
Council adopted the Striking Committee report as amended, confirming committee and board appointments for the new term.

The adopted report names Councillors Johnston and Schnider to lead Community & Infrastructure Services, Davey and Ioannidis to lead Finance & Corporate Services, and Singh and Chapman to lead Planning & Strategic Initiatives.
The adopted report fills citizen and council seats on advisory committees, the Committee of Adjustment, Kitchener Public Library, Kitchener Housing Inc. and Centre in the Square.
The adopted report exempts one Economic Development Advisory Committee member from the maximum years of service in the appointments policy.
The adopted report authorizes councillors to serve on Association of Municipalities of Ontario and Federation of Canadian Municipalities boards, with attendance expenses covered.

debate: There was no recorded debate on the motions. The hospital board amendment and the Striking Committee report each went to a vote with no discussion in the transcript.
In the inaugural address, the mayor said residents' top concerns, from the election, a survey and strategic planning input, were housing affordability, homelessness, climate change and road safety.

The mayor also urged civility and unity after the pandemic. The mayor encouraged residents to take part through the strategic plan, citizen committees, delegations, Engage Kitchener and public meetings.

A community reflection speaker, who works with a local interim housing community, said people experiencing homelessness want to be remembered. The speaker urged leaders to recognize everyone's humanity and keep a hopeful outlook.

The faith leaders' invocations asked council to act with wisdom, love and service. One asked that Kitchener be a place of safety and hospitality for everyone, citing support for people arriving from Ukraine.
